extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of algebraic topology (advanced undergraduate/graduate level)
extracted.subtask_description: Chapter-level textbook exposition of fundamental groups, homotopy, higher homotopy groups, covering projections, and the correspondence between subgroups of π1 and covering spaces. Contains definitions, theorems, examples, and lifting/regularity criteria used to compute π1 and classify coverings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundamental groups don't depend on basepoint
rubrics_metrics.description: Let X be a path-connected space. Then for any x1 ∈ X and x2 ∈ X, we have π1(X, x1) ≅ π1(X, x2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given any path α from x1 to x2 with reverse ᾱ, the isomorphism is induced by [γ] ↦ [α * γ * ᾱ]. This map is a homomorphism because (α * γ1 * ᾱ) * (α * γ2 * ᾱ) = α * γ1 * γ2 * ᾱ as α * ᾱ is nulhomotopic. The inverse is defined similarly using ᾱ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abuse of notation: π1(X) for path-connected spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: For a path-connected space X we often abbreviate π1(X, x0) to just π1(X), since it doesn’t matter which x0 ∈ X we pick.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to simplify notation once independence on basepoint is established.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simply connected iff π1 trivial
rubrics_metrics.description: Let X be a path-connected space. X is simply connected if and only if π1(X) is the trivial group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One direction is easy (trivial π1 implies any loop nullhomotopic); the other direction requires showing that any two paths with the same endpoints are homotopic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basepoint-preserving continuous map
rubrics_metrics.description: By f : (X, x0) → (Y, y0) we mean that f : X → Y is continuous and sends the point x0 to y0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This shorthand is used throughout when discussing induced maps on fundamental groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Induced map f♯ on loops / homotopy invariance
rubrics_metrics.description: Given f : (X, x0) → (Y, y0) and a loop γ in X at x0, composition f ◦ γ is a loop in Y at y0, denoted f♯γ. If γ1 ≃ γ2 (path-homotopic), then f♯γ1 ≃ f♯γ2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus f induces a well-defined group homomorphism f♯ : π1(X,x0) → π1(Y,y0). The homotopy invariance follows by composing the homotopy with f.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homeomorphism implies isomorphic fundamental groups
rubrics_metrics.description: If X and Y are homeomorphic (via basepoint-preserving homeomorphisms), then their fundamental groups are isomorphic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If f : X → Y and g : Y → X are inverse continuous maps with f(x0)=y0 and g(y0)=x0, then f♯ and g♯ are inverse group isomorphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loop as map S1 → X and definition of higher homotopy groups
rubrics_metrics.description: A loop is the same as a continuous function S1 → X. For general n, πn(X) is defined as the homotopy classes of maps Sn → X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Group operation for πn uses decompositions of [0,1]^n with endpoints/faces identified; for n ≥ 2 the groups πn(X) are abelian.

rubrics_metrics.name: πn(Sn) isomorphic to Z
rubrics_metrics.description: For each n, πn(Sn) ≅ Z.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This generalizes the π1(S1) ≅ Z intuition: maps of Sn can be classified by an integer degree (wrapping number).

rubrics_metrics.name: πn(Sm) is trivial when n < m
rubrics_metrics.description: If n < m then πn(Sm) is the trivial group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geometric intuition: a smaller-dimensional sphere can be contracted on the surface of a larger sphere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of homotopy between continuous functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Let f, g : X → Y be continuous. A homotopy is a continuous F : X × [0,1] → Y with F0(x) = f(x) and F1(x) = g(x) for all x ∈ X. If such F exists, f and g are homotopic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This generalizes path-homotopy (where domain is [0,1]) to arbitrary domain spaces; homotopies may not fix 'endpoints' unless specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homotopy equivalence of spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: Spaces X and Y are homotopy equivalent if there exist continuous f : X → Y and g : Y → X such that f ◦ g is homotopic to idY and g ◦ f is homotopic to idX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If X is homotopy equivalent to a point, X is called contractible. Homotopy equivalence is a weaker notion than homeomorphism but preserves many algebraic-topological invariants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homotopy equivalent spaces have isomorphic πn
rubrics_metrics.description: If X and Y are path-connected and homotopy-equivalent, then πn(X) ≅ πn(Y) for every positive integer n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maps f and g witnessing the homotopy equivalence induce inverse homomorphisms on πn, yielding isomorphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pointed homotopy category hTop*
rubrics_metrics.description: The pointed homotopy category hTop* has objects: pointed spaces (X,x0), and morphisms: homotopy classes of continuous functions (X,x0) → (Y,y0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two path-connected spaces are isomorphic in hTop* exactly when they are homotopy equivalent; this categorical viewpoint bundles homotopy information neatly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundamental group as functor π1 : hTop* → Grp
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a functor π1 sending (X,x0) to π1(X,x0) and a (homotopy class of a) map f to the induced homomorphism f♯.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functoriality implies composition-respecting induced maps, homotopic maps produce equal induced maps, and functors preserve isomorphisms (so isomorphic objects in hTop* have isomorphic π1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evenly covered open set
rubrics_metrics.description: Let p : E → B be continuous. An open set U ⊆ B is evenly covered by p if p^{-1}(U) is a disjoint union of open sets in E, each of which is mapped homeomorphically onto U by p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geometric intuition: U's preimage is a bunch of disjoint 'copies' (pancakes) each homeomorphic to U; not every open set must be evenly covered (e.g. whole space may fail).

rubrics_metrics.name: Covering projection (covering map)
rubrics_metrics.description: A covering projection p : E → B is a surjective continuous map such that every b ∈ B has an open neighborhood U ∋ b which is evenly covered by p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some authors omit surjectivity because if B is connected and E nonempty the evenly-covered condition forces surjectivity. Typical examples: R → S1 by θ ↦ e^{2πiθ}, z ↦ z^n on S1, exp : C → C\\{0}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image-of-p is union of components if p not assumed surjective
rubrics_metrics.description: If p : E → B satisfies the evenly-covered condition but is not assumed surjective, then the image of p is a disjoint union of connected components of B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus when B is connected and E nonempty, p must be surjective — motivating optional omission of surjectivity in some definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lifting of a path
rubrics_metrics.description: Given γ : [0,1] → B and p : E → B a covering projection, a lifting is a path ˜γ : [0,1] → E with p ◦ ˜γ = γ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpreting loops in B as paths in E via lifts can simplify π1 computations (e.g., lifting loops in S1 to R).

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence and uniqueness of path lifts (Lifting paths theorem)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose γ : [0,1] → B with γ(0)=b0 and p : (E,e0) → (B,b0) is a covering projection. Then there exists a unique lifting ˜γ : [0,1] → E such that ˜γ(0)=e0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses compactness of [0,1] to cover by finitely many evenly-covered neighborhoods and constructs the lift interval-by-interval; uniqueness follows from local homeomorphism property on each evenly-covered slice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locally path-connected space
rubrics_metrics.description: A space Y is locally path-connected if at any point x ∈ Y, every open neighborhood U of x contains a path-connected open neighborhood V ⊆ U.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This condition is required in the general lifting criterion for maps from spaces Y; many common spaces satisfy it.

rubrics_metrics.name: General lifting criterion for maps from Y
rubrics_metrics.description: Let p : (E,e0) → (B,b0) be a covering projection. If Y is path-connected and locally path-connected, then for any continuous f : (Y,y0) → (B,b0), a lifting ˜f with ˜f(y0)=e0 exists iff f♯(π1(Y,y0)) ⊆ p♯(π1(E,e0)). If a lifting exists, it is unique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation: the image subgroup of π1(Y) under f must lie inside the image subgroup of π1(E) under p. p♯ is injective, so p♯(π1(E,e0)) can be viewed as a subgroup of π1(B,b0).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lifting homotopies
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a homotopy γ1 ≃ γ2 in the base space B, one can lift it to a homotopy ˜γ1 ≃ ˜γ2 in E when appropriate lift conditions hold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special case: [0,1]×[0,1] is simply connected, so homotopies between paths lift; more generally lifting homotopies follows from lifting criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local path-connectedness is necessary (counterexample)
rubrics_metrics.description: The locally path-connected condition in the lifting theorem is necessary: there exist simply connected spaces Y (e.g., the Warsaw circle) and maps f : Y → S1 that do not lift to R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Warsaw circle is simply connected but not locally path-connected at the origin; collapsing the sine-curve vertically to S1 fails to lift, illustrating necessity of the hypothesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Endpoint correspondence Φ: π1(B,b0) → p^{-1}(b0)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a covering projection p : (E,e0) → (B,b0), define Φ([γ]) = ˜γ(1), where ˜γ is the unique lift starting at e0. This yields a function Φ : π1(B,b0) → p^{-1}(b0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If E is path-connected then Φ is surjective; if E is simply connected then Φ is injective. For universal covers (E simply connected) this identifies π1(B) with the fiber set, often giving group structure (e.g., π1(S1) ↔ Z).

rubrics_metrics.name: Universal cover
rubrics_metrics.description: A universal cover of a space B is a covering projection p : E → B where E is simply connected (hence path-connected).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often one says E is 'the' universal cover when p is understood. The universal cover corresponds to the trivial subgroup of π1(B) and covers every other covering space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular coverings from group actions
rubrics_metrics.description: If a group G acts continuously on a space X with trivial stabilizers and one forms the quotient projection X → X/G (identifying orbits), then this projection is a regular covering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Z acts on R by n·x = n+x giving R/ Z ≅ S1 and the projection R → S1 is regular. Regular coverings correspond to normal subgroups in the subgroup-cover correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Injectivity of p♯ for covering projections
rubrics_metrics.description: Let p : (E,e0) → (B,b0) be a covering projection of path-connected spaces. Then the homomorphism p♯ : π1(E,e0) → π1(B,b0) is injective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: if γ is nulhomotopic in B then its lift is nulhomotopic in E by lifting the homotopy; hence kernel of p♯ is trivial and p♯(π1(E)) embeds as a subgroup of π1(B).

rubrics_metrics.name: Map/isomorphism of covering projections
rubrics_metrics.description: Given two coverings p1 : E1 → B and p2 : E2 → B, a map of covering projections is a continuous f : E1 → E2 with p2 ◦ f = p1. Two coverings are isomorphic if there exist mutual inverse maps of covering projections between them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This lets one treat coverings as objects in a category; classification theorems identify covering spaces up to isomorphism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locally connected space
rubrics_metrics.description: A space X is locally connected if for each point x ∈ X and each open neighborhood V of x there is a connected open set U with x ∈ U ⊆ V.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a mild condition often satisfied in common spaces and appears in the subgroup-cover correspondence theorem hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semi-locally simply connected
rubrics_metrics.description: A space X is semi-locally simply connected if for every point x ∈ X there is an open neighborhood U such that all loops in U are nulhomotopic (the contraction need not take place in U).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This condition rules out pathological local loop behavior and, together with local connectedness, ensures covering-space classification by subgroups of π1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence: subgroups of π1 ↔ path-connected coverings; normals ↔ regular coverings
rubrics_metrics.description: If B is locally connected and semi-locally simply connected then: (i) every subgroup H ⊆ π1(B) corresponds to exactly one (up to isomorphism) path-connected covering p : E → B with image p♯(π1(E)) = H; (ii) normal subgroups of π1(B) correspond exactly to regular covering projections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This theorem allows complete translation between group-theoretic data of π1(B) and the topology/algebra of covering spaces; the universal cover corresponds to the trivial subgroup.
